rows.query: Commerce clients need a network API boundary for storefront and back-office functionality.
The platform must expose commerce capabilities to storefronts and admin clients through network APIs.
Swap external commerce infrastructure independently while keeping the main platform intact.
Third-party commerce services must be replaceable without rebuilding the whole platform.
CRM users need to maintain business records, saved views, and process flows.
Users must be able to manage CRM objects, views, and workflows.
Long-running CRM operations should not block interactive web requests.
Asynchronous CRM work must run outside the request-serving process.
External clinical applications need authorized REST and FHIR access to health data.
Healthcare information must be exposed to authorized applications through REST and FHIR interfaces.
Clinical interoperability requires the FHIR version four and SMART on FHIR standards.
The healthcare interface must support FHIR R4 and SMART-on-FHIR profiles.
Learners and teachers need core education features while offline.
The platform must provide teaching and learning functions without an Internet connection.
Disconnected facilities need selected records synchronized with peers or the central portal.
Partitioned facility data must synchronize with peer instances or the data portal.
Digital-twin state should be searchable and able to communicate with outside systems.
The system must maintain searchable twin state and exchange messages with external systems.
Clients should use digital twins independently of each physical device protocol.
Applications must interact with twins without depending on the device connection protocol.
The cloud backend needs adapters that collect readings and events from device protocols.
Device telemetry and events must be ingested through protocol adapters.
Commands from applications need delivery to the protocol adapter for the chosen device.
Application commands must be routed to the adapter connected to the target device.
Clients need a remote semantic-web endpoint for querying RDF data with SPARQL.
RDF datasets must be exposed through a network-accessible SPARQL service.
RDF data stored on an external mount must remain after the service container stops.
Persistent datasets must survive server-container termination when mounted outside it.
The scheduler needs a DAG model for tasks with dependencies.
Dependent work must be represented as directed acyclic workflows and tasks.
Workflow owners need API and UI controls to examine, start, and troubleshoot runs.
Operators must inspect, trigger, and debug workflows through an API and user interface.
Messaging servers need federation that synchronizes and resolves events with peer servers.
The system must exchange and reconcile events with other homeservers.
High-volume deployments should add worker replicas without scaling every other service.
Large installations must scale worker processes horizontally and independently.
Map editors need XML and JSON APIs for changing OpenStreetMap records.
XML and JSON interfaces must be exposed for editing OpenStreetMap data.
Users need to upload and retrieve GPS exchange traces.
The system must accept and expose GPX trace uploads.
The reporting platform needs ingestion across browser, text message, email, feed, and social sources.
Information must be collected from web, SMS, email, feeds, and social channels.
Incoming reports need normalization, classification, and geographic positioning.
Collected information must be transformed, categorized, and geolocated as posts.
The billing system needs to turn product usage into metered revenue amounts.
Usage events must be converted into billable metrics and charges.
Billing must create customer invoices and manage collecting the money owed.
The platform must generate invoices and coordinate payment collection.
Email, media processing, webhook delivery, and imports should execute asynchronously away from requests.
Non-request work such as email, image processing, webhooks, and catalog import must run as background jobs.
High-traffic commerce deployments need memory caching for costly calculations.
The platform must support caching expensive computations and an in-memory cache for high-traffic installations.
Business applications need customizable RBAC and privacy policy enforcement.
The platform must support flexible role-based security and configurable privacy controls.
An API-first business platform must connect to outside services and peer installations.
The platform must remain integrable with external services and other instances through its API-centric design.
Public-health data collection must work across web, Android, basic phones, and text messages.
Program data must be captured, managed, and validated from browser, Android, feature-phone, and SMS clients.
Health-program users need analytical dashboards, pivot views, charts, and maps.
The system must provide dashboards, pivots, charts, GIS, and other analytics visualizations.
The education platform needs personalized spaces for teachers, managers, and students.
Educators, administrators, and learners must create and use personalized learning environments.
Administrators need a common control surface for built-in and add-on plugins.
The platform must expose one unified management interface for standard and extension plugin types.
The social network must federate with separately administered ActivityPub instances.
The system must interoperate with independently operated ActivityPub servers.
New social posts should reach followers' timelines through background delivery.
Published statuses must be distributed asynchronously to recipient timelines.
The platform needs lifecycle management for subscriptions and periodic charges.
The system must manage recurring subscriptions and their billing.
Subscription updates need durable event and notification queues for coordination.
Billing changes must be coordinated over notification and persistent event queues.
Civil-registration country systems need event operations through tRPC and some REST APIs.
The event service must manage custom events and expose tRPC plus selected REST endpoints for country integrations.
A gateway should dispatch incoming requests to identity, event, and document backends.
The gateway must route client requests to authentication, event, and document services.
The IoT platform needs MQTT, REST, and WebSocket connectivity through agents and managers.
Devices must connect through protocol agents and manager APIs including MQTT, HTTP/REST, and WebSocket.
Device and asset automation should be driven by conditional, flow-based, and scripted rules.
Asset behavior must be automated through when-then, flow, and script rules.
The catalog needs multiple ingestion modes for metadata sources, including pull and push.
Metadata must be ingested from external systems through pull, push, synchronous, and asynchronous mechanisms.
A metadata change log should drive refreshed search and graph views.
Committed metadata changes must update search and graph projections from the change log.
Non-specialists need to import, find, publish, and map geographic datasets.
Users must upload, publish, discover, and visualize geospatial data and metadata.
Geospatial services need shared OAuth2 identity and access decisions with the main platform.
Authentication and authorization must be synchronized across GeoNode and pluggable geospatial services using OAuth2.
Commerce capabilities should be split into independently replaceable catalog, cart, order, and checkout modules.
Catalog, cart, order, and checkout behavior must execute through independent commerce modules.
Externally hosted extensions need durable API and webhook integration contracts.
Remote app backends must communicate through stable API and webhook contracts.
CRM customizations need independently deployable server, module, and UI packages.
Backend, module, and frontend extensions must be packaged independently.
CRM jobs triggered by schedules should execute in background workers, not web requests.
Scheduled workflows and asynchronous tasks must run outside interactive requests.
Edge data needs configurable pipelines for conversion, filtering, and routing.
Messages must be transformed, filtered, and routed through configurable processing pipelines.
The edge system must buffer data and forward it later when connectivity is unreliable.
Store-and-forward behavior must be retained for intermittent connectivity.
The processing service should turn drone imagery into maps, point clouds, terrain models, and 3D products.
Aerial image sets must produce georeferenced maps, point clouds, elevation models, and 3D outputs.
Automatic job placement should choose the available processing worker with the shortest queue.
The system must select an online processing node with the lowest queue when automatic selection is enabled.
Scientific jobs need routing to specialized handlers and selectable compute backends.
Submitted jobs must be assigned to dedicated handlers and configurable execution destinations.
Remote scientific jobs must keep their tracking state after the web server restarts.
Cluster-submitted jobs must remain trackable across a Galaxy server restart.
Researchers need dataset discovery, sharing, citation, and long-term preservation.
The repository must support sharing, finding, citing, and preserving research datasets.
Large table imports and search indexing should be handled by background workers.
Tabular ingestion and indexing work must execute asynchronously.
A self-hosted collaboration service needs file storage, sync, and sharing.
Users must store, synchronize, and share files and collaboration data.
Multiple application instances need a common distributed cache in a cluster.
Clustered deployments must share one distributed cache and support multiple application replicas.
Messaging clients need both HTTP APIs and long-lived WebSocket sessions.
The platform must expose REST APIs and persistent WebSocket connections to supported clients.
Reliable team messaging requires redundant app, database, and load-balancer components.
The deployment must maintain service through redundant application, database, and load-balancing infrastructure.
